newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: Costa Rica downscales coffee losses from hurricane.
newsitem.headline: Costa Rica downscales coffee losses from hurricane.

text.p: Just five percent of the 1996-97 Costa Rica coffee crop was lost through damage caused by Hurricane Cesar, the executive director of the Costa Rica Coffee Institute (ICAFE) said Thursday.

Downscaling earlier loss estimates of up to 20 percent losses of the crop which this upcoming cycle is seen producing 3.1 million 46-kg bags, Guillermo Canet added the losses were those registered to date and stressed the problems Cesar caused have not all been resolved.
"Losses registered to date total 145,000 bags (of 46-kg), but if works to repair access roads to the plantations are not completed in time, losses could be worse," Canet told Reuters.
Hurricane Cesar smashed through Costa Rica a month ago and caused widespread damage both to beans and infrastructure, killing 41 people and causing total damage estimated at $200 million.
Canet said the government is working flat out to repair roads and bridges in the regions worst affected, including the coffee growing zones of Los Santos, Perez Zeledon and Coto Brus.
Alonso Lara, the president of ICAFE, had initially calculated losses at 600,000 bags. But after detailed technical on-the-ground reports the estimates have been cut.
Before the storm damage, Costa Rica's crop estimates for this cycle (October 1 to September 30) were already down between 8 and 10 percent on the 3.4 million 46-kg bags produced in 1995-1996.
